newsitem.title: USA: Conn. Pequot tribe launches speedy casino ferry.
newsitem.headline: Conn. Pequot tribe launches speedy casino ferry.

text.p: The Mashantucket Pequot Indian tribe on Wednesday launched what they said was the fastest ferryboat in the U.S., to carry patrons from New York City to their Foxwoods Casino in Ledyard, Conn.
The vessel, named the Sassacus, can handle 302 passengers at speeds of 47 knots, or 54 miles per hour.
It will go into service in late summer or early autumn, after completing sea trials and certification by the U.S. Coast Guard, a tribal spokesman told Reuters.
The 400-member tribe last year set up a subsidiary, Pequot River Shipworks, to build and sell the ferryboats.
The shipbuilding unit now has 84 employees, the spokesman said.
The Pequots also said Wednesday that they have sold a vessel to an Argentinian company, Buquebus, which intends to ferry passengers from Naples and Fort Myers, Florida, to Key West, Florida.
The vessels are priced at $11 million, the spokesman said.
They are designed by a British company, FBM Marine Group.
The ferryboats use a tri cat design, which has two hulls in the water and a middle hull usually above the water.
The Pequots' Foxwoods Casino is the largest casino and gaming space in North America, with some 200,000 square feet of gaming space. It opened in 1992.
The tribe's reservation lands are held in trust by the federal government.
The Pequots last year earned $600 million in slot machine revenue, of which 25 percent or $150 million went to the state of Connecticut.
The Pequots plan to operate several ferryboats in the future, to serve patrons in New York, Boston, and other locations, the spokesman said.
